subject: Recap + DPA clarifications / next steps
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Laura Chen <laura.chen@harborbank.com>, James O'Neill <james.oneill@harborbank.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 28 Apr 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Recap: Call re: DPA questions and next steps

Hi Laura / James —

Thanks again for taking the time this morning. Quick recap from our call and the open items we should follow up on: 

1) Roles: Redwood would act as a data processor for the Harbor Bank integration; Harbor Bank remains the data controller for customer data. We'll reflect that clearly in the DPA (see attached HarborBank_DPA_v1.pdf and a short Redwood_DPA_Summary.docx).

2) Subprocessors: We discussed our standard subprocessors (cloud infra, telemetry/metrics, and managed logging). I'll attach the current subprocessors list and link to the public list. If Harbor needs any subprocessors excluded for compliance reasons, let me know and we can escalate.

3) Breach notice: Our standard practice is to provide initial notification within 72 hours of confirming a data incident, with follow-up updates as investigations proceed. If Harbor requires a different contractual SLA (e.g., 48 hours), please flag that and we can review with legal.

4) Data residency: Redwood supports region-specific hosting. For EU-only processing we can offer regional hosting options (hosted EU or Private deployment). Please confirm whether specific datasets must remain in eu-west-1.

5) PII & retention: Default inference KV cache is purged after 30 days; customers can configure retention via the console or opt for no retention. We provide audit logs and tokenization controls to limit exposure. Please share any mandated retention windows.

6) Logging & access controls: We provide per-user audit logs, role-based access, and optional encrypted logs with KMS-integrations. SOC 2 Type II and penetration test reports are available under NDA / via our compliance portal.

Next steps / asks from Harbor: 
- Please confirm which of the above (subprocessors, breach SLA, data residency, retention windows) Harbor wants changed in the DPA or require a call with Legal.
- If helpful, we can schedule a 30 min legal + security call early next week to walk through redlines.

Attachments: HarborBank_DPA_v1.pdf, Redwood_DPA_Summary.docx

Thanks,
Marissa Cole
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0123

From: Laura Chen <laura.chen@harborbank.com>

Cc: James O'Neill <james.oneill@harborbank.com>
Date: Wed, 28 Apr 2027 10:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Recap: Call re: DPA questions and next steps

Hi Marissa —

Thanks for the summary and the materials. A few quick clarifications from our side: 

- Controller/Processor: good to confirm that Harbor Bank will remain the controller. We just want that spelled out in the DPA (section which party controls data and which is processing).
- Subprocessors: can you share the specific list (company names) and whether Redwood requires Harbor sign-off before onboarding new subprocessors? We have policy restrictions around certain analytics vendors.
- Breach notice: Harbor's baseline requirement is notification within 48 hours of discovery for confirmed incidents impacting customer PII. Would Redwood be able to commit to 48 hours?
- Data residency: Harbor has a requirement that customer PII for EU customers stays within EU regions; is there a way for us to scope processing lanes to eu-west-1 only?
- SOC 2 / evidence: can you point us to how to request the SOC 2 report and any penetration test summaries?

James (cc'd) is our lead on vendor security — he'll likely want to jump on the legal call.

Can you send an updated DPA that shows the controller/processor language and the current subprocessors list? Ideally we'd get that before the legal call so we can pre-review redlines.

Best,
Laura
Director, IT Risk & Security | Harbor Bank
laura.chen@harborbank.com | +1 (617) 555-0199

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Laura Chen <laura.chen@harborbank.com>, James O'Neill <james.oneill@harborbank.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 28 Apr 2027 11:30:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Recap: Call re: DPA questions and next steps

Hi Laura / James —

Really appreciate the clear asks — below are specific responses and actions we'll take immediately: 

- Controller/Processor language: we will update the DPA to clearly state Harbor Bank as Controller and Redwood Inference as Processor in the definitions and recitals (we've highlighted the relevant clause in the attached HarborBank_DPA_v1.pdf).

- Subprocessors: our current subprocessors are: AWS (hosting/compute), Google Cloud (backup/analytics), Segment (telemetry), Datadog (metrics), and Sentry (error telemetry). We maintain a published list here: https://secure.redwood.ai/compliance/subprocessors-list. Standard practice is to notify customers 30 days prior to adding a new subprocessor; if Harbor requires explicit consent we can note that as a negotiation point.

- Breach notice SLA: Redwood's security practice is to provide an initial notification within 72 hours of confirming a data incident and to provide timely updates. That said, for confirmed incidents where there is clear evidence of customer PII exposure we can commit to providing initial notification within 48 hours -- we'll flag that as a proposed DPA amendment for Harbor to review.

- Data residency: we support region-restricted processing for hosted accounts and can offer EU-only processing via our EU region or via a Private deployment. I'll add language to the DPA about contractual data residency commitments and make a note about deployment options & timeline (hosting in eu-west-1 typically available within 2-4 weeks depending on provisioning).

- SOC 2 and evidence: SOC 2 Type II and latest pentest summary are available via our compliance portal; I've requested a share link for Harbor and will send an NDA-protected access link in a separate email.

Next steps from Redwood:
- I'll circulate an updated DPA that highlights the controller/processor language, subprocessors clause, breach-notice SLA (including proposed 48-hour option), and data residency language by EOD today.
- If Harbor can provide the specific retention windows and any subprocessors that are disallowed, Ben (cc'd) and I will incorporate those as redline items for the legal call.

Proposed times for a 30-min legal + security call: Thu 2027-04-29 10:00am PT or Thu 2027-04-29 2:00pm PT. Do either work?

Thanks -- attaching the updated DPA (HarborBank_DPA_v1.pdf) and a 1-page summary.

Regards,
Marissa
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference

James will forward any additional vendor security checklist items prior to the call.
